doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Crusaders, Chick Corea, Sondheim and Boston Pops collaborations
summary: She recalls The Way It Goes, a Sondheim duet and the Boston Pops.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You’ve done some unusual collaborations, unusual in that they were just one-offs. You did some things with the Crusaders.
That was big. That was big. What was the name of the song? It was big. I know that.
It went right out of my head.
Oh, I sang it for years. Oh God – what? – The Way It Goes?
Whew. That would have broken my heart, if I didn’t remember that. That was – that got – that was big for the Crusaders. That was big.
Who else did I work with?
There was some unusual compil- – Chick Corea, Return to Forever.
I’m glad that you’re remembering – have all this written down.
You were invited to do one or two songs, [Stephen] Sondheim, in the collection, which was . . .
That was where Peabo Bryson came in. It was a Sondheim song we did together. Don’t ask me the name of the song.

But when you mentioned Sondheim, I remembered, that was where Peabo Bryson came in, and I don’t remember the name of the song. [The duet was Loving You on Color and Light: Jazz Sketches on Sondheim, Sony 1995]
There was the Boston Pops. That was a recording.
Yes. It was fun. That’s my big orchestra. That’s my milieu.
